props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Indicates if Accordion support multiple Panels opened at the same time.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Callback to be called when the opened items change.

props.name: openItems
props.description: Controls the state of the panel.

hooks.

props.name: button
props.description: The component to be used as button in heading

props.name: expandIcon
props.description: Expand icon slot rendered before (or after) children content in heading.

props.name: expandIconPosition
props.description: The position of the expand  icon slot in heading.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.description: Expand icon slot rendered before (or after) children content in heading.

props.name: inline
props.description: Indicates if the AccordionHeader should be rendered inline.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of spacing in the heading.

props.description: Disables opening/closing of panel.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: icon
props.defaultValue: `PersonRegular` (the default icon's size depends on the Avatar's size)
props.description: Icon to be displayed when the avatar doesn't have an image or initials.

props.name: image
props.description:
The Avatar's image.

Usage e.g.: `image={{ src: '...' }}`

props.name: initials
props.description:
(optional) Custom initials.

It is usually not necessary to specify custom initials; by default they will be derived from the `name` prop,
using the `getInitials` function.

The initials are displayed when there is no image (including while the image is loading).

props.name: name
props.description:
The name of the person or entity represented by this Avatar. This should always be provided if it is available.

The name is used to determine the initials displayed when there is no image. It is also provided to
accessibility tools.

AvatarGroup.description: The AvatarGroup component displays a group of Avatars, each represented as an AvatarGroupItem.

The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:

point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout the AvatarGroupItems should be displayed as.

AvatarGroupItem.description:
The AvatarGroupItem component represents a single person or entity.
AvatarGroupItem should only be used in an AvatarGroup component.

props.name: active
props.description:
Optional activity indicator
* active: the avatar will be decorated according to activeAppearance
* inactive: the avatar will be reduced in size and partially transparent
* unset: normal display

props.name: activeAppearance
props.description: The appearance when `active="active"`

props.name: avatar
props.description: Avatar that represents a person or entity.

props.name: badge
props.description: Badge to show the avatar's presence status.

props.name: color
props.description:
The color when displaying either an icon or initials.
* neutral (default): gray
* brand: color from the brand palette
* colorful: picks a color from a set of pre-defined colors, based on a hash of the name (or idForColor if provided)
* [AvatarNamedColor]: a specific color from the theme

a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: icon
props.defaultValue: `PersonRegular` (the default icon's size depends on the Avatar's size)
props.description: Icon to be displayed when the avatar doesn't have an image or initials.

props.name: idForColor
props.description:
Specify a string to be used instead of the name, to determine which color to use when color="colorful".
Use this when a name is not available, but there is another unique identifier that can be used instead.

props.name: image
props.description:
The Avatar's image.

Usage e.g.: `image={{ src: '...' }}`

props.name: initials
props.description:
(optional) Custom initials.

It is usually not necessary to specify custom initials; by default they will be derived from the `name` prop,
using the `getInitials` function.

The initials are displayed when there is no image (including while the image is loading).

props.name: name
props.description:
The name of the person or entity represented by this Avatar. This should always be provided if it is available.

The name is used to determine the initials displayed when there is no image. It is also provided to
accessibility tools.

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description:
Label used for the name of the AvatarGroupItem when rendered as an overflow item.
The content of the label, by default, is the `name` prop from the `avatar` slot.

AvatarGroupPopover.description: The AvatarGroupPopover component provides a button with a Popover containing the children provided.

props.name: appearance
props.description:
A popover can appear styled with brand or inverted.
When not specified, the default style is used.

props.name: closeOnIframeFocus
props.description: Flag to close the Popover when an iframe outside a PopoverSurface is focused

props.name: closeOnScroll
props.description: Close when scroll outside of it

props.name: content
props.description: List that contains the overflowed AvatarGroupItems.

props.name: count
props.description:
Number of AvatarGroupItems that will be rendered.

Note: AvatarGroupPopover handles counting the number of children, but when using a react fragment to wrap the
children, this is not possible and therefore it has do be added manually.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Used to set the initial open state of the Popover in uncontrolled mode

props.name: indicator
props.description:
Whether the triggerButton should render an icon instead of the number of overflowed AvatarGroupItems.
Note: The indicator will default to `icon` when the size is less than 24.

props.name: inertTrapFocus
props.description:
Enables standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal)
where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert,
making navigation leak from the trapped area back to the browser toolbar and vice-versa.

props.name: inline
props.description: Popovers are rendered out of DOM order on `document.body` by default, use this to render the popover in DOM order

props.name: legacyTrapFocus
props.description:
Must be used with the `trapFocus` prop
Enables older Fluent UI focus trap behavior where the user
cannot tab into the window outside of the document. This is now
non-standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal)
where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert.
@deprecated this behavior is default provided now, to opt-out of it in favor of standard behavior use the `inertTrapFocus` property

props.name: mountNode
props.defaultValue: a new element on document.body without any styling
props.description: Where the portal children are mounted on DOM

props.name: mouseLeaveDelay
props.description: Sets the delay for closing popover on mouse leave

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description:
Call back when the component requests to change value
The `open` value is used as a hint when directly controlling the component

props.name: open
props.description: Controls the opening of the Popover

props.name: openOnContext
props.description: Flag to open the Popover as a context menu. Disables all other interactions

props.name: openOnHover
props.description: Flag to open the Popover by hovering the trigger

props.name: popoverSurface
props.description: PopoverSurface that contains the content.

props.name: positioning
props.description:
Configures the position of the Popover.
Explore [Positioning docs](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/concepts-developer-positioning-components--docs) for more options.

props.name: size
props.description: Determines popover padding and arrow size

props.name: surfaceMotion
props.description:
Slot for the surface motion animation.
For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip shown when triggerButton is hovered.

props.name: trapFocus
props.description: Should trap focus

props.name: triggerButton
props.description: Button that triggers the Popover.

props.name: unstable_disableAutoFocus
props.description:
By default Popover focuses the first focusable element in PopoverSurface on open.
Specify `disableAutoFocus` to prevent this behavior.

props.name: withArrow
props.description: Display an arrow pointing to the target.

props.name: appearance
props.description:
A Badge can be filled, outline, ghost, inverted
@defaultvalue filled

props.name: color
props.description:
A Badge can be one of preset colors
@defaultvalue brand

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: size

A Badge can be on of several preset sizes.
@defaultvalue medium

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: iconPosition
props.description:
A Badge can position the icon before or after the content.
@defaultvalue before

props.name: overflowCount
props.description: Max number to be displayed

props.name: shape
props.description: A Badge can be circular or rounded

props.name: showZero
props.description: If the badge should be shown when count is 0

props.name: size
props.description:
A Badge can be on of several preset sizes.
@defaultvalue medium

props.name: focusMode
props.description:
Sets the focus behavior for the Breadcrumb.

`tab`
This behaviour will cycle through all elements inside of the Breadcrumb when pressing the Tab key and then release focus
after the last inner element.

`arrow`
This behaviour will cycle through all elements inside of the Breadcrumb when pressing the Arrow key.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

BreadcrumbItem.description:
BreadcrumbItem component is a wrapper for BreadcrumbLink and BreadcrumbButton.
It can be used as a non-interactive item.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls size of Breadcrumb items and dividers.

Button.description: Buttons give people a way to trigger an action.

props.name: appearance
props.description:
A button can have its content and borders styled for greater emphasis or to be subtle.
- 'secondary' (default): Gives emphasis to the button in such a way that it indicates a secondary action.
- 'primary': Emphasizes the button as a primary action.
- 'outline': Removes background styling.
- 'subtle': Minimizes emphasis to blend into the background until hovered or focused.
- 'transparent': Removes background and border styling.

props.name: disabledFocusable
props.description:
When set, allows the button to be focusable even when it has been disabled.
This is used in scenarios where it is important to keep a consistent tab order
for screen reader and keyboard users. The primary example of this
pattern is when the disabled button is in a menu or a commandbar and is seldom used for standalone buttons.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon that renders either before or after the `children` as specified by the `iconPosition` prop.

props.name: menuIcon
props.description: Menu icon that indicates that this button has a menu that can be expanded.

SplitButton.description:
SplitButtons are a grouping of two interactive surfaces where interacting with the first one triggers a primary
action, while interacting with the second one opens a menu with secondary actions.

props.name: disabledFocusable
props.description:
When set, allows the button to be focusable even when it has been disabled.
This is used in scenarios where it is important to keep a consistent tab order
for screen reader and keyboard users. The primary example of this
pattern is when the disabled button is in a menu or a commandbar and is seldom used for standalone buttons.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon that renders either before or after the `children` as specified by the `iconPosition` prop.

props.name: iconPosition
props.description: A button can format its icon to appear before or after its content.

props.name: menuIcon
props.description: Menu icon that indicates that this button has a menu that can be expanded.

ToggleButton.description: A button component that can be toggled between checked and unchecked states.

props.name: checked
props.description:
Defines the controlled checked state of the `ToggleButton`.
If passed, `ToggleButton` ignores the `defaultChecked` property.
This should only be used if the checked state is to be controlled at a higher level and there is a plan to pass the
correct value based on handling `onClick` events and re-rendering.

props.name: disabledFocusable
props.description:
When set, allows the button to be focusable even when it has been disabled.
This is used in scenarios where it is important to keep a consistent tab order
for screen reader and keyboard users. The primary example of this
pattern is when the disabled button is in a menu or a commandbar and is seldom used for standalone buttons.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: logo
props.description: Container that holds a logo related to the image preview provided.

Carousel.description:
Carousel is the context wrapper and container for all carousel content/controls,
it has no direct style or slot opinions.

Carousel also provides API interfaces for callbacks that will occur on navigation events.

props.name: activeIndex
props.description: The value of the currently active page.

props.name: align
props.description: The alignment of the carousel.

props.name: announcement
props.description:
Localizes the string used to announce carousel page changes
Defaults to: undefined

props.name: appearance
props.description:
Sets visual treatment for the Carousel container.

`flat`
Retains the minimal styling used by default prior to introducing appearance-based styles.

`elevated`
Applies rounded corners, background, and shadow tokens so the Carousel is presented as a surfaced container.

props.name: autoplayInterval
props.description:
Choose a delay between autoplay transitions in milliseconds.
Only active if Autoplay is enabled via CarouselAutoplayButton

Defaults: 4000

props.name: circular
props.description: Circular enables the carousel to loop back around on navigation past trailing index.

props.name: defaultActiveIndex
props.description: The initial page to display in uncontrolled mode.

The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: groupSize
props.description:
Controls the number of carousel cards per navigation element, will default to 'auto'
Recommended to set to '1' when using full page carousel cards.

props.name: motion
props.description:
Sets motion type as either 'slide' or 'fade'
Defaults: 'slide'

Users can also pass 'slide' & duration via CarouselMotion object to control carousel speed.
Drag interactions are not affected because duration is then determined by the drag force.

Note: Duration is not in milliseconds because Carousel uses an
attraction physics simulation when scrolling instead of easings.
Only values between 20-60 are recommended, 25 is the default.

props.name: onActiveIndexChange
props.description: Callback to notify a page change.

props.name: whitespace
props.description:
Adds whitespace to start/end so that 'align' prop is always respected for current index
Defaults to: False

CarouselCard.description:
The defining wrapper of a carousel's indexed content, they will take up the full
viewport of CarouselSlider or div wrapper,
users may place multiple items within this Card if desired, with consideration of viewport width.

Clickable actions within the content area are available via mouse and tab as expected,
non-active card content will be set to inert until moved to active card.

props.name: autoSize
props.description: Sets the card styling to be responsive based on content.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: totalSlides
props.description:
The total number of slides available.
Users may override if using the component without a Carousel wrapper or implementing custom functionality.

CarouselNavButton.description: The child element of CarouselNav, a singular button that will set the carousels active value on click.

props.name: disabledFocusable
props.description:
When set, allows the button to be focusable even when it has been disabled.
This is used in scenarios where it is important to keep a consistent tab order
for screen reader and keyboard users. The primary example of this
pattern is when the disabled button is in a menu or a commandbar and is seldom used for standalone buttons.

props.name: layout
props.description:
Default: 'inline'
Defines the nav container layout:

'inline' - Default controls inline with carousel view

 inline-wide - Similar to inline but places nav buttons on far left/right

'overlay' - Controls overlaid on bottom of carousel viewport,

'overlay-wide' - Controls overlaid on bottom of carousel viewport with prev+autoplay/next buttons on far side

'overlay-expanded' - Controls overlaid on bottom of carousel viewport, with prev/next buttons on sides vertically centered

CarouselNavImageButton.description:
A variant child element of CarouselNav, a singular image button that displays a
preview of card content and will set the carousels active value on click.

props.name: disabledFocusable
props.description:
When set, allows the button to be focusable even when it has been disabled.
This is used in scenarios where it is important to keep a consistent tab order
for screen reader and keyboard users. The primary example of this
pattern is when the disabled button is in a menu or a commandbar and is seldom used for standalone buttons.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: image
props.description: Required: The image within the button

props.name: cardFocus
props.description:
cardFocus sets the carousel slider as a focus group,
enabling left/right navigation of elements.

This will also be passed into CarouselCards via context and set the appropriate focus attributes

Defaults: false

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Triggers a callback when the value has been changed. This will be called on every individual step.

props.name: shape
props.description:
ColorPicker shape
@defaultvalue 'rounded'

props.name: transparency
props.description:
The `transparency` property determines how the alpha channel is interpreted.
- When `false`, the alpha channel represents the opacity of the color.
- When `true`, the alpha channel represents the transparency of the color.
For example, a 30% transparent color has 70% opacity.
@defaultvalue false

props.name: vertical
props.description: Render the Slider in a vertical orientation, smallest value on the bottom.

props.name: color
props.description: The current color of the ColorArea.

props.name: defaultColor
props.description: The starting value for an uncontrolled ColorArea.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Triggers a callback when the value has been changed. This will be called on every individual step.

props.name: shape
props.description:
ColorPicker shape
@defaultvalue 'rounded'

props.name: vertical
props.description: Render the Slider in a vertical orientation, smallest value on the bottom.

props.name: clearable
props.description: If set, the combobox will show an icon to clear the current value.

props.description: The dropdown clear icon

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The default open state when open is uncontrolled

props.name: defaultSelectedOptions
props.description:
For an uncontrolled component, sets the initial selection.
If this is set, the `defaultValue` prop MUST also be set.

props.description: Disable auto-focusing on the first item when mounting.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: input
props.description: The primary slot, an input with role="combobox"

props.name: listbox
props.description: The dropdown listbox slot

props.name: multiselect
props.description:
Sets the selection type to multiselect.
Set this to true for multiselect, even if fully controlling selection state.
This enables styles and accessibility properties to be set.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the open/closed state of the dropdown changes

props.name: onOptionSelect
props.description: Callback when an option is selected

props.name: open
props.description:
Sets the open/closed state of the dropdown.
Use together with onOpenChange to fully control the dropdown's visibility

props.name: root
props.description: The root combobox slot

props.name: selectedOptions
props.description:
An array of selected option keys.
Use this with `onOptionSelect` to directly control the selected option(s)
If this is set, the `value` prop MUST also be controlled.

Dropdown.description: Dropdown component - TODO: add more docs

props.name: button
props.description: The primary slot, the element with role="combobox"

props.name: clearable
props.description: If set, the combobox will show an icon to clear the current value.

props.name: clearButton
props.description: The dropdown clear icon

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The default open state when open is uncontrolled

props.name: defaultSelectedOptions
props.description:
For an uncontrolled component, sets the initial selection.
If this is set, the `defaultValue` prop MUST also be set.

props.name: disableAutoFocus
props.description: Disable auto-focusing on the first item when mounting.

props.name: expandIcon
props.description: The dropdown arrow icon

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: text
props.description:
An optional override the string value of the Option's display text,
defaulting to the Option's child content.
This is used as the Dropdown button's or Combobox input's value when the option is selected,
and as the comparison for type-to-find keyboard functionality.
The string value of the Option's display text when the Option's children are not a string.
This is used as the Dropdown button's or Combobox input's value when the option is selected,
and as the comparison for type-to-find keyboard functionality.

props.name: value
props.description:
Defines a unique identifier for the option.
Use this to control selectedOptions, or to get the option value in the onOptionSelect callback.
Defaults to `text` if not provided.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: label
props.description:
The option group label, displayed as static text before the child options.
If not using label, it's recommended to set `aria-label` directly on the OptionGroup instead.

props.name: allFocusable
props.description: Allows all elements to be focused, including disabled ones

props.name: allowTextInput
props.description: Whether the DatePicker allows input a date string directly or not

props.name: borderless
props.description: Determines if the DatePicker has a border.

props.name: dateTimeFormatter
props.description: Apply additional formatting to dates, for example localized date formatting.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the DatePicker should be open by default

props.name: disableAutoFocus
props.description:
Whether the DatePicker should open automatically when the control is focused
WARNING: setting this to false creates an accessibility violation and is not recommended

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disabled state of the DatePicker.

props.name: firstDayOfWeek
props.description: The first day of the week for your locale.

props.name: firstWeekOfYear
props.description:
Defines when the first week of the year should start, FirstWeekOfYear.FirstDay,
FirstWeekOfYear.FirstFullWeek or FirstWeekOfYear.FirstFourDayWeek are the possible values

props.name: formatDate
props.description: Optional method to format the chosen date to a string to display in the DatePicker

props.name: highlightCurrentMonth
props.description: Whether the month picker should highlight the current month

props.name: highlightSelectedMonth
props.description: Whether the month picker should highlight the selected month

props.name: initialPickerDate
props.description: The initially highlighted date.

props.name: inlinePopup
props.description: Whether the DatePicker should render the popup as inline or in a portal

props.name: isMonthPickerVisible
props.description: Whether the month picker is shown beside the day picker or hidden.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: The maximum allowable date.

props.name: minDate
props.description: The minimum allowable date.

props.name: mountNode
props.defaultValue: a new element on document.body without any styling
props.description: Where the portal children are mounted on DOM

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback to run when the DatePicker's open state changes

props.name: onSelectDate
props.description: Callback issued when a date is selected

props.name: onValidationResult
props.description: Callback to run after the DatePicker's input has been validated

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the DatePicker is open or not

props.name: openOnClick
props.description: Whether the DatePicker should open when the input is clicked

props.name: parseDateFromString
props.description: Optional method to parse the text input value to date, it is only useful when allowTextInput is set to true

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the DatePicker

props.name: positioning
props.description: Configure the positioning of the DatePicker dialog

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the DatePicker is a required field or not. When using `<Field>`, this prop is automatically set.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Whether the CalendarDay close button should be shown or not.

props.name: showGoToToday
props.description: Whether the "Go to today" link should be shown or not

props.name: showMonthPickerAsOverlay
props.description: Show month picker on top of date picker when visible.

props.name: showWeekNumbers
props.description: Whether the calendar should show the week number (weeks 1 to 53) before each week row

props.name: strings
props.description: Localized strings to use in the Calendar

props.name: today
props.description: Value of today. If unspecified, current time in client machine will be used.

props.name: underlined
props.description: Whether or not the Input of the DatePicker is underlined.

props.name: value
props.description:
Default value of the DatePicker, if any

When the component is controlled, `null` should be used instead of `undefined` to avoid controlled vs. uncontrolled
ambiguity.

Dialog.description:
The `Dialog` root component serves as an interface for all Dialog behaviors.
It provides context to compound sub-components: `DialogTrigger`, `DialogSurface`,
`DialogHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogBody`, and `DialogActions`.

This component uses the native HTML `<dialog>` element (via `DialogSurface`) for
built-in focus trapping, backdrop, and accessibility semantics.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Default value for the uncontrolled open state of the dialog.

props.name: inertTrapFocus
props.description:
Enables standard behavior according to the HTML dialog spec
where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert.
Native `<dialog showModal()>` always uses inert focus trapping,
so this prop is accepted for API parity but does not change behavior.

props.name: modalType
props.description:
Dialog variations.

`modal`: When this type of dialog is open, the rest of the page is dimmed out and cannot be interacted with.
The tab sequence is kept within the dialog. This is the default type of the component.

`non-modal`: When a non-modal dialog is open, the rest of the page is not dimmed out
and users can interact with the rest of the page.

`alert`: is a special type of modal dialog that interrupts the user's workflow
to communicate an important message or ask for a decision.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the component changes value from open state.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls the open state of the dialog.

props.name: unmountOnClose
props.description: Decides whether the dialog should be removed from the DOM when it is closed.

DialogActions.description:
`DialogActions` is a container for the actions of the dialog.
Apart from styling, this component does not have other behavior.

props.name: fluid
props.description: Makes the actions expand the entire width of the DialogBody

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

DialogSurface.description:
DialogSurface component represents the visual part of a `Dialog` as a whole,
it contains everything that should be visible.

props.name: backdrop
props.description:
Dimmed background of dialog.
The default backdrop is rendered as a `<div>` with styling.
This slot expects a `<div>` element which will replace the default backdrop.
The backdrop should have `aria-hidden="true"`.

Accepts an `appearance` prop to control backdrop visibility:
- `'dimmed'`: Always shows a dimmed backdrop, regardless of nesting.
- `'transparent'`: Always shows a transparent backdrop.
@example ```tsx
<DialogSurface backdrop={{ appearance: 'dimmed' }} />
```

DialogTrigger.description:
A non-visual component that wraps its child
and configures them to be the trigger that will open or close a `Dialog`.
This component should only accept one child.

This component sole purpose is to avoid opting out of the internal controlled open state of a `Dialog`
Besides being a trigger that opens/close a dialog through context this component doesn't do much,
making it basically unnecessary in cases where the trigger is outside of the `Dialog` component.

props.name: action
props.description:
Explicitly declare if the trigger is responsible for opening or
closing a Dialog visibility state.

If `DialogTrigger` is outside `DialogSurface` then it'll be `open` by default

If `DialogTrigger` is inside `DialogSurface` then it'll be `close` by default

props.name: disableButtonEnhancement
props.description: Disables internal trigger mechanism that ensures a child provided will be a compliant ARIA button.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: modalType
props.description:
Dialog variations.

`modal`: When this type of dialog is open, the rest of the page is dimmed out and cannot be interacted with.
The tab sequence is kept within the dialog. This is the default type of the component.

`non-modal`: When a non-modal dialog is open, the rest of the page is not dimmed out
and users can interact with the rest of the page.

`alert`: is a special type of modal dialog that interrupts the user's workflow
to communicate an important message or ask for a decision.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the component changes value from open state.

props.name: position
props.description:
Position of the drawer.

Note: 'bottom' does not supports size, but it supports customized height.

props.name: type
props.description:
Type of the drawer.
Type of the drawer.

- 'overlay' - Drawer is hidden by default and can be opened by clicking on the trigger.
- 'inline' - Drawer is stacked with the content.

props.name: unmountOnClose
props.description:
Decides whether the dialog should be removed from the DOM when it is closed.
Decides whether the drawer should be removed from the DOM tree when it is closed.
This can be useful when dealing with components that may contain state that should not
be reset when the drawer is closed.

DrawerBody.description: DrawerBody provides with a container for the main content of a Drawer.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls the open state of the Drawer

props.name: position
props.description:
Position of the drawer.

Note: 'bottom' does not supports size, but it supports customized height.

props.name: separator
props.description: Whether the drawer has a separator line.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size of the drawer.

- 'small' - Drawer is 320px wide.
- 'medium' - Drawer is 592px wide.
- 'large' - Drawer is 940px wide.
- 'full' - Drawer is 100vw wide.

props.name: unmountOnClose
props.description:
Decides whether the drawer should be removed from the DOM tree when it is closed.
This can be useful when dealing with components that may contain state that should not
be reset when the drawer is closed.

OverlayDrawer.description: OverlayDrawer contains supplementary content and are used for complex creation, edit, or management experiences.

props.name: backdrop
props.description:
Dimmed background of dialog.
The default backdrop is rendered as a `<div>` with styling.
This slot expects a `<div>` element which will replace the default backdrop.
The backdrop should have `aria-hidden="true"`.

Accepts an `appearance` prop to control backdrop visibility:
- `'dimmed'`: Always shows a dimmed backdrop, regardless of nesting.
- `'transparent'`: Always shows a transparent backdrop.
@example ```tsx
<DialogSurface backdrop={{ appearance: 'dimmed' }} />
```

props.name: backdropMotion
props.description: For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
@deprecated OverlayDrawer can work only as a controlled component
and does not support uncontrolled mode i.e. defaultOpen prop

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: inertTrapFocus
props.description:
Enables standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal)
where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert.

props.name: modalType
props.description:
Dialog variations.

`modal`: When this type of dialog is open, the rest of the page is dimmed out and cannot be interacted with.
The tab sequence is kept within the dialog and moving the focus outside
the dialog will imply closing it. This is the default type of the component.

`non-modal`: When a non-modal dialog is open, the rest of the page is not dimmed out
and users can interact with the rest of the page.
This also implies that the tab focus can move outside the dialog when it reaches the last focusable element.

`alert`: is a special type of modal dialogs that interrupts the user's workflow
to communicate an important message or ask for a decision.
Unlike a typical modal dialog, the user must take an action through the options given to dismiss the dialog,
and it cannot be dismissed through the dimmed background.

props.name: mountNode
props.defaultValue: a new element on document.body without any styling

props.name: onOpenChange
open

props.name: position
props.description:
Position of the drawer.

Note: 'bottom' does not supports size, but it supports customized height.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size of the drawer.

- 'small' - Drawer is 320px wide.
- 'medium' - Drawer is 592px wide.
- 'large' - Drawer is 940px wide.
- 'full' - Drawer is 100vw wide.

props.name: surfaceMotion
props.description: For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

props.name: unmountOnClose
props.description:
Decides whether the drawer should be removed from the DOM tree when it is closed.
This can be useful when dealing with components that may contain state that should not
be reset when the drawer is closed.

The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: hint
props.description: Additional hint text below the field.

props.name: label
props.description: The label associated with the field.

props.name: required
props.description:
Marks the Field as required. If `true`, an asterisk will be appended to the label, and `aria-required` will be set
on the Field's child.

props.name: validationMessage
props.description:
A message about the validation state. By default, this is an error message, but it can be a success, warning,
or custom message by setting `validationState`.

props.name: validationMessageIcon
props.description:
The icon associated with the `validationMessage`. This will only be displayed if `validationMessage` is set.

The default depends on `validationState`:
* error: `<ErrorCircle12Filled />`
* warning: `<Warning12Filled />`
* success: `<CheckmarkCircle12Filled />`
* none: `null`

props.name: validationState
props.defaultValue: error when validationMessage is set; none otherwise.
props.description:
The `validationState` affects the display of the `validationMessage` and `validationMessageIcon`.

* error: (default) The validation message has a red error icon and red text, with `role="alert"` so it is
    announced by screen readers. Additionally, the control inside the field has `aria-invalid` set, which adds a
    red border to some field components (such as `Input`).
* success: The validation message has a green checkmark icon and gray text.
* warning: The validation message has a yellow exclamation icon and gray text, with `role="alert"` so it is
    announced by screen readers.
* none: The validation message has no icon and gray text.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: info
props.description: The content of the InfoButton's popover.

props.name: infoButton
props.description:
The InfoButton component.

It is not typically necessary to use this prop. The content can be set using the `info` prop of the InfoLabel.

props.name: label
props.description:
The Label component.

It is not typically necessary to use this prop. The label text is the child of the `<InfoLabel>`, and other props
such as `size` and `required` should be set directly on the `InfoLabel`.

This is the PRIMARY slot: all native properties specified directly on `<InfoLabel>` will be applied to this slot,
except `className` and `style`, which remain on the root slot.

props.name: required
props.description:
Displays an indicator that the label is for a required field. The required prop can be set to true to display
an asterisk (*). Or it can be set to a string or jsx content to display a different indicator.

Input.description: The Input component allows people to enter and edit text.

props.name: appearance
props.defaultValue:
'outline'

Note: 'filled-darker-shadow' and 'filled-lighter-shadow' are deprecated and will be removed in the future.
props.description: Controls the colors and borders of the input.

props.name: contentAfter
props.description: Element after the input text, within the input border

props.name: contentBefore
props.description: Element before the input text, within the input border

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
Default value of the input. Provide this if the input should be an uncontrolled component
which tracks its current state internally; otherwise, use `value`.

(This prop is mutually exclusive with `value`.)

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: input
props.description:
The actual `<input>` element. `type="text"` will be automatically applied unless overridden.

This is the "primary" slot, so native props specified directly on the `<Input>` will go here
(except `className` and `style`, which go to the `root` slot). The top-level `ref` will
also go here.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the user changes the input's value.

props.name: root
props.description:
Wrapper element which visually appears to be the input and is used for borders, focus styling, etc.
(A wrapper is needed to properly position `contentBefore` and `contentAfter` relative to `input`.)

The root slot receives the `className` and `style` specified directly on the `<Input>`.
All other top-level native props will be applied to the primary slot, `input`.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the input (changes the font size and spacing).

props.name: type
props.description:
An input can have different text-based [types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/Input#input_types)
based on the type of value the user will enter.

Note that no custom styling is currently applied for alternative types, and some types may
activate browser-default styling which does not match the Fluent design language.

(For non-text-based types such as `button` or `checkbox`, use the appropriate component or an
`<input>` element instead.)

props.name: value
props.description:
Current value of the input. Provide this if the input is a controlled component where you
are maintaining its current state; otherwise, use `defaultValue`.

(This prop is mutually exclusive with `defaultValue`.)

InteractionTag.description:
InteractionTag component - a visual representation of an attribute with primary and secondary actions.
Can have `InteractionTagPrimary` and `InteractionTagSecondary` components as its children.

props.name: appearance
props.description: An InteractionTag can have filled, outlined or brand experience.

props.name: disabled
props.description: An InteractionTag can show that it cannot be interacted with.

props.name: required
props.description:

an asterisk (*). Or it can be set to a string or jsx content to display a different indicator.

props.description: A label supports regular and semibold fontweight.

props.name: appearance
props.description:
A link can appear either with its default style or subtle.
If not specified, the link appears with its default styling.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the link is disabled.

props.name: disabledFocusable
props.description:
When set, allows the link to be focusable even when it has been disabled. This is used in scenarios where it is
important to keep a consistent tab order for screen reader and keyboard users.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: inline
props.description: If true, changes styling when the link is being used alongside other text content.

Menu.description: Wrapper component that manages state for a popup MenuList and a MenuTrigger

props.name: checkedValues
props.description: Map of all checked values

props.name: closeOnScroll
props.description: Close when scroll outside of it

props.name: defaultCheckedValues
props.description: Default values to be checked on mount

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the popup is open by default

props.name: hasCheckmarks
props.description: States that menu items can contain selectable items and reserve slots for item alignment

props.name: hasIcons
props.description: States that menu items can contain icons and reserve slots for item alignment

props.name: hoverDelay
props.description: Sets the delay for mouse open/close for the popover one mouse enter/leave

props.name: inline
props.description:
Root menus are rendered out of DOM order on `document.body`, use this to render the menu in DOM order
This option is disregarded for submenus

props.name: mountNode
props.defaultValue: a new element on document.body without any styling
props.description: Where the portal children are mounted on DOM

props.name: onCheckedValueChange
onOpenChange
props.type: (e: MouseEvent | Event | React.MouseEvent<...> | React.MouseEvent<...> | KeyboardEvent<...> | TouchEvent, data: MenuOpenChangeData) => void
props.description:
Call back when the component requests to change value
The `open` value is used as a hint when directly controlling the component

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popup is open

props.name: openOnContext
props.description: Opens the menu on right click (context menu), removes all other menu open interactions

props.name: openOnHover
props.description: Opens the menu on hover

props.name: persistOnItemClick
props.description: Do not dismiss the menu when a menu item is clicked

props.name: positioning
props.description: Configures the positioned menu

props.name: surfaceMotion
props.description:
Slot for the surface motion animation.
For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

props.name: bottomReflowSpacer
props.description:
Rendered when the component is in multiline layout to guarantee correct spacing even
if no actions are rendered. When actions are rendered, the default actions grid area will render
over this element

NOTE: If you are using this slot, this probably means that you are using the MessageBar without
actions, this is not recommended from an accesibility point of view

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: defaultOpenCategories
props.description:
Set of categories that are opened by default.
Typically useful when the openCategories is uncontrolled.

props.name: defaultSelectedCategoryValue
props.description:
The value of the navCategory to be selected by default.
Typically useful when the selectedValue is uncontrolled.
Mutually exclusive with selectedValue.
Empty string indicates no selection.

props.name: defaultSelectedValue
props.description:
The value of the navItem to be selected by default.
Typically useful when the selectedValue is uncontrolled.
Mutually exclusive with selectedValue.
Empty string indicates no selection.

props.description: The vertical density of the Nav and it's children

a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:

point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute

props.name: name
props.description:
The name of the person or entity represented by the Persona.

When `primaryText` is not provided, this will be used as the default value for `primaryText`.

props.name: presence
props.description:
PresenceBadge to display.

If `presenceOnly` is true, the PresenceBadge will be displayed instead of the Avatar.

props.name: presenceOnly
props.description: Whether to display only the presence.

props.name: primaryText
props.description:
The first line of text in the Persona, larger than the rest of the lines.

`primaryText` defaults to the `name` prop. We recomend to only use `name`, use `primaryText` when the text is
 different than the `name` prop.

props.name: quaternaryText
props.description: The fourth line of text in the Persona.

props.name: secondaryText
props.description: The second line of text in the Persona.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of a Persona and its text.

props.name: tertiaryText
props.description: The third line of text in the Persona.

props.name: textAlignment
props.description: The vertical alignment of the text relative to the avatar/presence.

props.name: textPosition
props.description: The position of the text relative to the avatar/presence.

Popover.description: Wrapper component that manages state for a PopoverTrigger and a PopoverSurface components.

props.name: appearance
props.description:
A popover can appear styled with brand or inverted.
When not specified, the default style is used.

props.name: closeOnIframeFocus
props.description: Flag to close the Popover when an iframe outside a PopoverSurface is focused

props.name: closeOnScroll
props.description: Close when scroll outside of it

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Used to set the initial open state of the Popover in uncontrolled mode

props.name: inertTrapFocus
props.description:
Enables standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal)
where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert,
making navigation leak from the trapped area back to the browser toolbar and vice-versa.

props.name: inline
props.description: Popovers are rendered out of DOM order on `document.body` by default, use this to render the popover in DOM order

props.name: legacyTrapFocus
props.description:
Must be used with the `trapFocus` prop
Enables older Fluent UI focus trap behavior where the user
cannot tab into the window outside of the document. This is now
non-standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal)
where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert.
@deprecated this behavior is default provided now, to opt-out of it in favor of standard behavior use the `inertTrapFocus` property

props.name: mountNode
props.defaultValue: a new element on document.body without any styling
props.description: Where the portal children are mounted on DOM

props.name: mouseLeaveDelay
props.description: Sets the delay for closing popover on mouse leave

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description:
Call back when the component requests to change value
The `open` value is used as a hint when directly controlling the component

props.name: open
props.description: Controls the opening of the Popover

props.name: openOnContext
props.description: Flag to open the Popover as a context menu. Disables all other interactions

props.name: openOnHover
props.description: Flag to open the Popover by hovering the trigger

props.name: positioning
props.description:
Configures the position of the Popover.
Explore [Positioning docs](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/concepts-developer-positioning-components--docs) for more options.

props.name: size
props.description: Determines popover padding and arrow size

props.name: surfaceMotion
props.description:
Slot for the surface motion animation.
For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

props.name: trapFocus
props.description: Should trap focus

props.name: unstable_disableAutoFocus
props.description:
By default Popover focuses the first focusable element in PopoverSurface on open.
Specify `disableAutoFocus` to prevent this behavior.

props.name: withArrow
props.description: Display an arrow pointing to the target.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: indeterminateMotion
props.description: Motion slot for the indeterminate animation. Pass `null` to disable the animation.

props.name: max
props.description:
The maximum value, which indicates the task is complete.
The ProgressBar bar will be full when `value` equals `max`.

props.name: shape
props.description: The shape of the bar and track.

props.name: thickness
props.description: The thickness of the ProgressBar bar

props.name: value
props.description:
A decimal number between `0` and `1` (or between `0` and `max` if given),
which specifies how much of the task has been completed.

If `undefined` (default), the ProgressBar will display an **indeterminate** state.

props.name: dir

props.name: targetDocument
props.description: Provides the document, can be undefined during SSR render.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: layout
props.description: How the radio items are laid out in the group.

props.name: name
props.description:
The name of this radio group. This name is applied to all Radio items inside this group.

If no name is provided, one will be generated so that all of the Radio items have the same name.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback when the selected Radio item changes.

props.name: required
props.description: Require a selection in this group. Adds the `required` prop to all child Radio items.

props.name: value
props.description:
The selected Radio item in this group.

This should be the `value` prop of one of the Radio items inside this group.

Rating.description: Rating is a wrapper for one or more rating items that will be used to set a rating value.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: input
props.description:
The actual `<input>` element. `type="text"` will be automatically applied unless overridden.

This is the "primary" slot, so native props specified directly on the `<Input>` will go here
(except `className` and `style`, which go to the `root` slot). The top-level `ref` will
also go here.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Custom onChange callback.
Will be traditionally supplied with a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> for usual character entry.
When the dismiss button is clicked, this will be called with an event of type React.MouseEvent<HTMLSpanElement>
and an empty string as the `value` property of the data parameter

props.name: root
props.description:
Wrapper element which visually appears to be the input and is used for borders, focus styling, etc.
(A wrapper is needed to properly position `contentBefore` and `contentAfter` relative to `input`.)

The root slot receives the `className` and `style` specified directly on the `<Input>`.
All other top-level native props will be applied to the primary slot, `input`.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the input (changes the font size and spacing).

props.name: type
props.description:
An input can have different text-based [types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/Input#input_types)
based on the type of value the user will enter.

Note that no custom styling is currently applied for alternative types, and some types may
activate browser-default styling which does not match the Fluent design language.

(For non-text-based types such as `button` or `checkbox`, use the appropriate component or an
`<input>` element instead.)

props.name: value
props.description:
Current value of the input. Provide this if the input is a controlled component where you
are maintaining its current state; otherwise, use `defaultValue`.

(This prop is mutually exclusive with `defaultValue`.)

props.name: appearance
props.description: Controls the colors and borders of the Select.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible

props.name: input
props.description:
The hidden input for the Slider.
This is the PRIMARY slot: all native properties specified directly on `<Slider>` will be applied to this slot,
except `className` and `style`, which remain on the root slot.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Triggers a callback when the value has been changed. This will be called on every individual step.

props.name: orient
props.description:
Orient is a non standard attribute that allows for vertical orientation in Firefox. It is set internally
when `vertical` is set to true.
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/range#non_standard_attributes
Webkit/Chromium support for vertical inputs is provided via -webkit-appearance css property

props.name: rail
props.description: The Slider's base. It is used to visibly display the min and max selectable values.

props.name: root
props.description:
The root of the Slider.
The root slot receives the `className` and `style` specified directly on the `<Slider>`.
All other native props will be applied to the primary slot, `input`.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the Slider.

props.name: thumb
props.description:
The draggable icon used to select a given value from the Slider.
This is the element containing `role = 'slider'`.

props.name: value
props.description:
The current value of the controlled Slider.
Mutually exclusive with `defaultValue` prop.

props.name: vertical
props.description: Render the Slider in a vertical orientation, smallest value on the bottom.

SpinButton.description: A SpinButton allows someone to incrementally adjust a value in small steps.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Controls the colors and borders of the input.

props.name: decrementButton
props.description: Renders the decrement control.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
Initial value of the control (assumed to be valid). Updates to this prop will not be respected.

Use this if you intend for the SpinButton to be an uncontrolled component which maintains its
own value. For a controlled component, use `value` instead. (Mutually exclusive with `value`.)

Use `null` to indicate the control has no value.

props.name: displayValue
props.description:
String representation of `value`.

Use this when displaying the value to users as something other than a plain number.
For example, when displaying currency values this might be "$1.00" when value is `1`.

Only provide this if the SpinButton is a controlled component where you are maintaining its
current state and passing updates based on change events. When SpinButton is used as an
uncontrolled component this prop is ignored.

props.description:
The `focusgroup` attribute is used to indicate that a group of elements should be treated as
a single focusable unit for keyboard navigation purposes. It can be used to create accessible
components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: focusgroupstart
props.description:
The `focusgroupstart` attribute is used to indicate that an element is the starting
point of a focus group. It can be used in conjunction with the `focusgroup` attribute
to create accessible components that support keyboard navigation and focus management.

props.name: incrementButton
props.description: Renders the increment control.

props.name: input
props.description:
Input that displays the current value and accepts direct input from the user.
Displayed value is formatted.

This is the primary slot.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Callback for when the committed value changes.
- User presses the up/down buttons (on single press or every spin)
- User presses the up/down arrow keys (on single press or every spin)
- User *commits* edits to the input text by focusing away (blurring) or pressing enter.
  Note that this is NOT called for every key press while the user is editing.

props.name: precision
props.description:
How many decimal places the value should be rounded to.

The default is calculated based on the precision of `step`: i.e. if step = 1, precision = 0.
step = 0.0089, precision = 4. step = 300, precision = 2. step = 23.00, precision = 2.

props.name: root
props.description:
The root element of SpinButton is a container `<div>`.
The root slot receives the `className` and `style` specified on the `<SpinButton>`.
All other native props are applied to the primary slot: `input`.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the input.

props.name: stepPage
props.description:
Large difference between two values. This should be greater than `step` and is used
when users hit the Page Up or Page Down keys.

props.name: value
props.description:
Current value of the control (assumed to be valid).

Only provide this if the SpinButton is a controlled component where you are maintaining its
current state and passing updates based on change events; otherwise, use the `defaultValue`
property.

Use `null` to indicate the control has no value.

Mutually exclusive with `defaultValue`.

props.name: appearance
props.description: The appearance of the Spinner.

props.name: delay
props.description: Time in milliseconds after component mount before spinner is visible.

props.name: shape

Swatch shape
@defaultvalue 'square'

props.name: size

Swatch size
@defaultvalue 'medium'

props.name: spacing

Switch.description: Switches enable users to trigger an option on or off through pressing the component.

props.name: checked
props.description:
Defines the controlled checked state of the Switch.
If passed, Switch ignores the `defaultChecked` property.
This should only be used if the checked state is to be controlled at a higher level and there is a plan to pass the
correct value based on handling `onChange` events and re-rendering.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Defines whether the Switch is initially in a checked state or not when rendered.

props.name: disabledFocusable
props.description:
When set, allows the Switch to be focusable even when it has been disabled. This is used in scenarios where it is
important to keep a consistent tab order for screen reader and keyboard users.
